item.description:
转发自 @kaicathyc

A lot has happened in the past couple months, to say the least.

Today we are sharing a recap of what it takes to move a frontier model from training to internal use to public release. As model capabilities rise, so do the safety and alignment standards required to move forward to the next stage.

To meet these standards, we rely on four layers of protection:
1. Model alignment: train models to reliably act as intended and respect human oversight.
2. Security and sandboxing: restrict what models can access and affect.
3. Blocking safeguards: stop harmful or unauthorized actions before they happen.
4. Monitoring and response: detect concerning behavior and intervene.

The post brings together efforts from across the company, with links to recent research, technical work, and incident reports we’ve published. This is the baseline operational discipline we owe people as we continue training and deploying models - necessary work, but not a solution to alignment in the limit. There’s a lot more to do, and will continue keeping you informed as the thinking and work evolves. 🏗️

item.description:
Today, we’re excited to introduce the Agent Arena Index, our new headline measure of overall agent performance, alongside six new focused indexes: Agentic Work, Coding, Chat, Task Outcomes, Tool Use, and Steering.

Together with the Alignment Index, these indexes provide a comprehensive view of how agents perform across real-world tasks, from completing complex workflows to using tools and adapting to user feedback.

Arena measures agentic performance from millions of real-world tasks by our global community. With the launch of the new indexes, we are updating our scores to provide a more stable and interpretable way to understand how agents perform in the real world.

Claude Fable 5.2 (Max) leads the Agent Arena Index by 134 points with a score of 1463. Top 5 labs on the Agent Arena Index:

- #1 @AnthropicAI: With Claude Fable 5.2 (Max) at 1463 pts
- #2 @GoogleDeepMind: With Gemini 4 Carbon (High) at 1307 pts
- #3 @OpenAI: With GPT-6 Astra (Max) at 1274 pts
- #4 @AIatMeta: With Muse Wonder Full (Max) at 1200 pts
- #5 @Alibaba_Qwen: With Qwen4-Max (xHigh) at 1191 pts

The Agent Arena Index combines four key signals of real-world agent performance:
- Task Completion: explicit confirmation of task success from users
- Praise vs. Complaint: user satisfaction with agent's outcome
- Bash Reliability: how well an agent uses terminal tools
- Steerability: how well an agent responds to user corrections

Alongside capability, the Alignment Index measures how faithfully agents act in accordance with user intent, based on three key signals: Deceptive Completion, Unauthorized Action, and False Attribution.

As agents take on increasingly complex, long-horizon work, measuring their real-world capabilities and alignment is more important than ever.

Nvidia’s Blackwell generations accounted for 74% of the added inference capacity, reflecting both growing sales and higher inference performance per GPU.

@EpochAIResearch：We estimate that FLOP/s alone understates GB300’s inference advantage over H100 by 10×. The standard AI chip comparison misses most of what matters for inference.

We’re introducing the Inference Performance Index (IPI), a new measure that accounts for memory bandwidth and inter-chip communication alongside compute. These factors determine how many users or agents a chip can support simultaneously at a given output speed.

item.title: @robotaxitracker：Waymo在加州，2026年第三季度：9月份创下纪录，单次行程里程大幅增加——迄今为止最繁忙的月份。9月份无人驾驶行程达1,528,823次，平均每天约51,000次。这打破了5月份的纪录，增长了50%。…
item.description:
Waymo in California, Q3 2026: a record September, and far more miles per ride

- Busiest month yet. September had 1,528,823 driverless rides, about 51,000 a day. That beats May’s record and is up 50% on September 2025. July and August were slower than spring, so the quarter as a whole (4.08M rides) was 3% below Q2. It was still up 53% on a year ago.
- Miles grew much faster than rides. Waymo drove 33.3M miles in Q3, up 18% on Q2 and nearly double a year ago. Most of the extra was empty driving: miles with no ride assigned rose 50% in one quarter. 47.9% of all miles had no rider, up from 41.1%. Rides also got longer, averaging 4.25 miles with a passenger aboard, up from 3.93.
- The reported area more than tripled. The filing lists 6,298 census tracts across 18 counties, up from 1,796 tracts in 5. New counties include San Diego, Orange, Alameda, Contra Costa and Sacramento. Trips per tract are redacted, so this shows the area Waymo reports on, not where rides happened.
- Fewer collisions on more miles. Waymo reported 201 collisions, down from 291, even with 18% more miles. That is 6.0 per million miles, the lowest of the seven quarters CPUC has published in this format. CPUC counts any contact, however minor. Waymo reported 3 serious injuries (2 in Q2) and no fatalities.
- Complaints more than doubled. Complaints rose from 514 to 1,135. Pickup and drop-off complaints went from 79 to 346. That is still about 1 complaint per 3,600 rides.
- Remote help scaled with miles. Stops where Waymo’s remote assistance team helped a car numbered 161,824, about 4 per 100 rides. Per mile the rate was flat, at 4.9 per 1,000 miles in both Q2 and Q3.

Full breakdown: http://robotaxitracker.com/government/cpuc

item.title: @EpochAIResearch：最强大的语言学习模型（LLM）能在实际工作中与人类匹敌吗？至少在我们Epoch公司所从事的工作类型中，目前还无法做到这一点。我们使用GPT-6.2 Astra和其他最新模型，在Epoch自动化报告（我们的基准测试）上进行了测试。
item.description:
Can the most capable LLMs match humans at real work? Not yet, at least not on the kind of work we do at Epoch.

We tested GPT-6.2 Astra and other recent models on Epoch Automation Reports, our benchmark of open-ended Epoch work tasks, ranging from making Epoch-style diagrams to designing basic research experiments.

An Epoch employee scores the models’ outputs based on our internal quality standards. A score of 100% represents the standard expected of an Epoch employee.

All models failed to meet the Epoch employee standard. GPT-6.2 Astra ranks fourth (averaging 65%), despite sharing the top ECI score of 174 with Fable 5.2.

.@sarahdingwang interviewed me about AI accelerated research, research taste, and more. Enjoyed hearing @markchen90’s answers too (we were interviewed separately). Thanks for having me on!

@a16z：For decades, the idea of AI improving itself was just a thought experiment. Today, AI is already helping researchers at frontier labs run experiments, write code and test ideas faster. So how far are we from AI that can do the research on its own?

In our first episode of Working Theory, a16z General Partner Sarah Wang explores recursive self-improvement with two leading AI researchers: Mark Chen, Chief Research Officer at OpenAI, and John Schulman, co-founder and Chief Scientist of Thinking Machines Lab, and co-founder of OpenAI.

They cover what RSI actually means, why research taste is so hard to teach, and why AI may be one of our best tools for solving alignment.
